::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 1st [1867]  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourn  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 181-182
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd)
I believe the childish form does not last,[^1] it is always cramping and a scratch of the pen will alter it where it prevails.

I was sorry afterwards I had not mentioned St John being recognised by his former pupil, the captain of the robbers, when he went out to be taken by him. It would be a fine subject for expression, and I wonder it has never been taken before. I believe I meant Archippus - the (supposed) angel of Laodicea as the third pupil of St John, but there is not enough of him to stand alone, without a wonderful amount of sermonizing - so I have worked him in with the other <s>less</s> little distinguished and half made out people.

 I hope you will put an Eagle on the [cover](organizations/other_167.qmd). Have you seen the Eagle in New College Chapel, it is a magnificent creature, and I should <u>most particularly</u> like to have it either there or in the title page, or both, for many reasons. I would send you a photograph but the one I have is not in the best position - and you are so much at Oxford that it would be sending coals to Newcastle.

What a fair and sensible [article](other_books/otherbook_498.qmd) Mr Ll. Davies’s is.

We are in a world of hayfields delicious to all senses

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

It is just possible that on Wednesday or Thursday [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd) may call on you.[^2] If you will be from home on either of those days - would you let her know at the [Revd W. Sewell](people/person_1306.qmd)’s

Huntley

Gloucester

---

[^1]: He had objected to the childish tone of her draft chapters of *The Pupils of St. John the Divine*.
[^2]: This would be in connection with the book of *Historical Selections* being compiled by CMY and Sewell.
